revisions: 1.0.1 — INSTRUMENT FIX ONLY, no prompt changed. Two expectation bugs found on the first live pass: (a) item 2's expectedAnswerKeywords required the phrase 'anticipatory bail', but BNSS 482's actual statutory title is 'Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest' — a correct answer using the statutory wording was scored as a quality shortfall, which is a defect in the instrument, not in the answer. Keyword entries may now be an array of accepted alternatives (any-of). (b) The same for item 1's reliance on a single phrasing. NOTE: prompts are untouched. Tuning a PROMPT to improve a result is forbidden; correcting a wrong expectation is required.
frozenNote: FROZEN SET — do not edit a prompt to improve a result. That is how a benchmark becomes marketing. Adding a class is allowed only as a NEW version file (v2) so before/after runs against v1 stay comparable. Every published figure must name the set version it was measured on.

baseline.rationale: The claim is 'NYV vs calling the model directly', so the baseline must be a real provider call, not a strawman. We deliberately use THE SAME MODEL the NYV router actually selects in production (measured §1.0: every class except mapping resolved to gemini-3-1-pro-preview), so answer-quality is equivalent by construction and the measured delta is attributable to orchestration alone rather than to a cheaper model.
baseline.systemInstructionNote: Deliberately none. 'Direct LLM' means the user's prompt with no scaffolding — that IS the alternative we are claiming to beat. Adding a system prompt would make the baseline more expensive and flatter NYV.
baseline.notCoveredNote: A single direct call is not a like-for-like substitute for a naive integration that ALSO retries, hedges, or fans out. Where a real integration would do that, the baseline understates direct cost, i.e. this comparison is conservative against NYV.

weighting.provenance: Derived from the traffic shares already committed in scripts/nv-cost-model.py (TODAY table), which are themselves an ASSUMED mix, not measured production traffic. Stated here so any blended figure can be re-blended against a different mix.
weighting.honestCaveat: These shares are an assumption. A blended cost figure is only as good as this table. If real nysdev/NSP traffic is ever sampled, replace this block in a v2 file and re-run — do not silently retune v1.
derivation: REALLOCATED: §1.0's 'classify/extract' 0.10 has no counterpart in §2.6's set, and §2.6's heavy classes (multi-issue, multi-jurisdiction swarm, long context) have no counterpart in §1.0. That 0.10 is reallocated to them: multi-issue-strategy 0.05, multi-jurisdiction-conflict 0.03, long-context 0.02.

ZERO-WEIGHT: cache-repeat and adversarial-scope carry weight 0. They are correctness probes. Excluding cache-repeat from the blend means the blended figure gives NYV NO credit for cache hits — deliberately conservative.

prompts.label: long context (fact matrix)
prompts.prompt:
Review the following factual matrix and advise on maintainability, forum and interim relief. Address each proceeding separately and then the interaction between them.

FACTS. The client, Mr. A, is an executive director of a company listed on the NSE and BSE. (1) A FIR was registered at Bandra police station, Mumbai, under BNS 318(4) and BNS 316(2) on the complaint of a minority shareholder, alleging that inter-corporate deposits placed with three related entities between FY2019-20 and FY2022-23 were a device to divert funds. The FIR names Mr. A as accused no. 2. No arrest has been made; a notice under BNSS 35(3) was served and answered. (2) The Directorate of Enforcement issued summons under PMLA section 50 to Mr. A in respect of the same transactions, treating the BNS 318(4) offence as the scheduled offence. A provisional attachment order under PMLA section 5 has been passed over a residential property held jointly with his spouse, who is not named in the FIR. The Adjudicating Authority has issued a notice under section 8. (3) SEBI issued a show-cause notice under the LODR Regulations and the PFUTP Regulations alleging non-disclosure of related-party transactions and misstatement in the audited financial statements for FY2020-21 and FY2021-22; SEBI has also passed an ex parte interim order restraining Mr. A from accessing the securities market. (4) A civil suit for recovery of Rs. 42 crore filed by a lender is pending before the Delhi High Court, in which a Order XXXVIII Rule 5 application for attachment before judgment is listed. (5) The company's audit committee obtained an independent forensic report which concluded that the deposits were commercially explicable but inadequately disclosed; the report has not been filed in any proceeding. (6) The transactions were disclosed in the audited financial statements and in the annual return, though not tagged as related-party transactions. (7) Limitation: the earliest transaction is dated 12 June 2019; the FIR was registered on 3 March 2026; the SEBI show-cause notice is dated 20 January 2026. (8) Mr. A is 58, has no prior criminal antecedents, holds an Indian passport, and has travelled abroad twice since the FIR with prior intimation to the investigating officer. QUESTIONS. (a) In which forum and in what sequence should anticipatory bail, quashing, PMLA appellate relief, and SEBI appellate relief be pursued? (b) What is the limitation exposure on each? (c) Does the spouse have an independent remedy against the section 5 attachment? (d) What is the risk that the forensic report becomes disclosable? (e) Does the pending civil suit create any prejudice in the criminal proceedings?
